instructions: Use KISS's official search interface at https://kiss.kstudy.com/. Observe the current DOM and accessible labels before choosing controls; there are no prevalidated selectors. Search the user's requested phrase and field scope exactly. When the interface only supports broad/full-text search, inspect each candidate title, abstract and author keywords and record exact match evidence; do not count a match found only in references or body text. Preserve result totals, record identifiers, result URLs, filters and pagination stop evidence. A bibliographic record is not a downloaded article. Determine original research eligibility from the journal's section/type and reported study methods, explicitly excluding reviews, editorials, letters without original data, theses and conference abstracts unless requested. Open each eligible record and follow its original/publisher link only within the mission's approved origins. Request a scope change if a required publisher origin is missing. Verify institutional entitlement or open availability before saving files. Inspect the article landing page and full text for supplementary material declarations and links; retain main/supplement roles and hashes using ORE artifact tools. A missing supplement link is unknown until the authoritative page has been inspected. Use exported citations only as metadata, never as full-text evidence. Record each unresolved access, challenge, unavailable PDF and supplement status. Stop at the requested verified count or exhaust the search with explicit evidence. Use the existing bounded challenge policy and preserve handoff checkpoints. Never fabricate eligibility or completion from a search snippet alone. Prefer a small public HTML fetch before opening a browser when the approved source allows it. KISS article detail pages observed on 2026-09-11 expose citation_title, citation_abstract and sometimes citation_doi meta tags even when earlier browser navigation failed. Re-check the current HTTP status and observed metadata; a previous 403 does not establish that every current detail request is blocked. A search shell without populated records is an unresolved inventory, not zero results. Download buttons and their current first-party script may expose an institution-authorized download action; use only the observed action and entitlement, never guessed file paths or invented access tokens.

context.content_model: Search result -> Bibliographic record -> Publisher record -> Main PDF and declared supplements
